scenes.text: What if reality doesn’t appear… it renders?
I need to tell you what I saw the night the room took ten seconds to load.
scenes.query: man sitting on couch dim room night

scenes.text: It started fast. One breath I was on my couch… the next, the walls stopped pretending to be solid.
scenes.query: colorful light patterns projected on face

scenes.text: They peeled back into a grid. Thin lines of light, stretching in every direction— like the blueprint underneath the paint.
And behind the grid… color.
Not color like you know it. Color that felt like it was looking back.
There was a presence there. I never saw its face.
I only felt it step aside… like an usher showing me into a theater I’d been sitting in my whole life without noticing.
scenes.query: empty theater red seats dramatic light

scenes.text: It didn’t speak in words. It spoke in showings.
scenes.query: projector light beam dust colorful dark

scenes.text: It showed me my bedroom, half-built.
Furniture appearing only when my attention touched it.
The hallway behind me… unrendered. Not dark. Just not yet.
And then it showed me the loading screen.
Every morning of my life. Those few gray seconds between sleeping and being someone.
scenes.query: person waking up bed soft gray morning light

scenes.text: Before my name arrives. Before my problems arrive.
Before the room finishes assembling around the story of me.
I always thought that blankness was nothing. It showed me that blankness is the canvas.
scenes.query: paint drop on white canvas color macro

scenes.text: Then—like a dimmer turned all the way up at once— I was back.
Same couch. Same ceiling. Same hands.
scenes.query: hands open palms close up dim light

scenes.text: But here’s what I can’t unsee.
The next morning, I caught it.
That gray moment before I became myself… and for two full seconds, I watched the world load.
scenes.query: defocused city morning coming into focus

scenes.text: You’ve felt it too. You just never called it anything.
scenes.query: person staring at ceiling lying bed

scenes.text: So tonight, notice it. Notice the half-second where a room finishes becoming a room.
scenes.query: lamp turning on warm room light

scenes.text: Notice how your name feels like something you put on.
scenes.query: person putting on jacket mirror morning

scenes.text: I’m not telling you the molecule showed me the truth. Maybe it only showed me the seams.
But now, every morning, in that gray and quiet gap… I remember what the presence never said out loud:
You are not waiting for reality. Reality is waiting for you.
Because you were never standing in the world… you were standing in the loading screen.
scenes.query: person standing glowing digital grid horizon
